summary:
MarsWalk is an interactive Martian map and pedestrian route planner built for the Interplanetary Survival Guide challenge. It combines global terrain data with more detailed elevation models where available to propose walking routes and scientific stops informed by geological maps.

The tool compares alternative routes, checks slopes and gaps in terrain data, identifies uncertain sections, and estimates travel time based on walking speed and terrain difficulty. Mission planning features include sunlight calculations and scenarios for temperature, wind, dust, radiation, and communications.

MarsWalk turns public planetary data into a practical way to explore route choices. Its central feature is transparency: users can see which terrain source supports each section and where further observations or human review are needed. It is an exploratory planning tool, not a certified navigation system for astronauts.
details:
MarsWalk is an interactive map and pedestrian route planner for Mars. Users can choose two locations to compare possible walking corridors, or start a science expedition from point A and select a geological target proposed by the app. The map combines a global MOLA terrain overview with USGS HRSC/MOLA elevation data and, where usable, more detailed CTX or HiRISE stereo terrain models. Route sections display their terrain source and uncertainty. The planner examines slope, elevation gaps, model boundaries, distance, and estimated walking time; it marks sections that need review instead of treating missing detail as proof of safe passage.

For science planning, MarsWalk displays mapped geological units and proposes observation targets near the route. A mission worksheet estimates travel and stop time, applies a terrain-related walking slowdown, and compares the plan with user-entered resource limits. It calculates geometric sunlight from the planned departure time. Temperature, wind, dust, radiation, and communication assessments use explicitly entered assumptions; the app does not claim a live, planet-wide forecast.

We built the browser application with JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Node.js, esbuild, and GeoTIFF processing tools. NASA and USGS planetary datasets provide the map and terrain information. OpenAI Codex assisted with research, implementation, debugging, interface design, and documentation; the team directed the work and reviewed the results. MarsWalk does not contain an AI model that predicts terrain passability.

The project's intended impact is to make planetary route planning more transparent. It helps explorers compare options and identify where better terrain observations or expert review are required. It is a research and planning prototype, not a certified astronaut navigation system.
